categories.main_business_segments: Asahi Co., Ltd. operates primarily in the bicycle business, encompassing the retail sale of bicycles, parts, and accessories, as well as related services such as maintenance and repair. The company manages a nationwide chain of directly operated stores, franchise stores, and an online sales platform. It also engages in wholesale distribution of its own and licensed brands to other retailers. The business is treated as a single segment focused on bicycles and related products and services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company focuses on the planning and development of its own branded bicycles and accessories, which are mainly manufactured by overseas partners in China and Taiwan. Asahi emphasizes quality control, requiring compliance with Japanese Industrial Standards (JIS) and its own safety and quality benchmarks. In-store assembly, maintenance, and repair are performed by certified staff, supported by internal training and a proprietary Meister certification system to ensure technical proficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Asahi serves a broad consumer base, including general users, families, sports cyclists, and children, through its retail stores and e-commerce channels. It also supplies products to other bicycle retailers and franchisees, and provides services to corporate and institutional clients. The company’s main markets are individuals seeking bicycles for daily use, leisure, or sports, as well as retail partners seeking quality bicycle products.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates 528 directly managed stores and 17 franchise stores across all regions of Japan, including Hokkaido, Tohoku, Kanto, Chubu, Kinki, Chugoku, Shikoku, and Kyushu. It also has a subsidiary in Beijing, China, and conducts some business activities in Taiwan through manufacturing partnerships. The vast majority of sales and assets are concentrated in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Asahi operates primarily at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer and service provider, but also has midstream activities through product planning, development, and wholesale distribution of its own and licensed brands. The company outsources manufacturing to overseas suppliers and manages logistics through its own distribution centers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include nationwide store expansion, enhancement of the OMO (Online Merges with Offline) strategy, and strengthening customer relationships through CRM and digital platforms. The company aims to increase the share of its own branded products, improve operational efficiency, and develop new store formats for urban markets. Sustainability, digital transformation, logistics optimization, and brand development are key themes, though there is no significant mention of traditional R&D activities.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through the sale of bicycles, parts, and accessories at retail stores and online. Additional income streams include service fees for maintenance and repairs, franchise royalties, wholesale sales to other retailers, and membership fees for customer programs. Revenue recognition is based on product delivery or service completion.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Asahi is positioned as Japan’s largest specialty bicycle retail chain and a leading SPA (Specialty store retailer of Private label Apparel) in the bicycle industry. Key competitors include other national and regional bicycle retailers, general merchandise stores with bicycle sections, and online bicycle sellers. The company differentiates itself through its nationwide network, proprietary brands, and integrated service offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending February 2025, Asahi reported sales of approximately 81.6 billion yen, with operating profit of 5.49 billion yen and net profit of 3.56 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in sales and profits, with a 4.5% year-on-year increase in revenue and a 14.2% increase in net profit. It maintains a strong financial position with high equity ratio (71.8%) and consistent investment in store expansion and infrastructure.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Asahi emphasizes reliable quality, value-for-money products, and comprehensive after-sales services, including maintenance, repair, and extended warranties. Its unique value lies in its nationwide store network, integrated online and offline customer experience, and the ability to offer both proprietary and leading international brands. The company also highlights its commitment to safety, sustainability, and customer lifestyle support, aiming to be a trusted partner in customers’ cycling lives.
